content.title: About
content.content: Reduced‑fat chocolate milk (2 % milk fat) is a beverage made from skimmed cow’s milk blended with cocoa powder, sugar, and flavorings. It delivers the creamy chocolate taste while providing far fewer calories and saturated fats than regular chocolate milk.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first chocolate milk was introduced in the United States in the early 20th century as a way to make chocolate more affordable.
Reducing the fat content to 2 % retains most of the calcium and vitamin D naturally present in milk.
The cocoa powder used is rich in flavonoids, which have antioxidant properties.
In many countries reduced‑fat chocolate milk is marketed as a “kids’ drink” to support growth and development.
Emulsifiers such as lecithin are often added to improve texture and prevent separation.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Even with reduced fat, the milk provides a high level of calcium essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Rich in vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D enhances calcium absorption and supports immune function.

items.title: Contains flavonoids
items.content: Cocoa powder supplies antioxidants that help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: At 2 % milk fat the beverage is lower in calories, making it suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Good protein source
items.content: Milk delivers high‑quality protein needed for tissue repair and muscle maintenance.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People who cannot digest lactose may experience bloating, gas, or diarrhea after consuming milk.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Added sugar gives the drink its sweet taste, which can be problematic for diabetics or those limiting sugar intake.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergic reactions to casein or whey can occur in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Caffeine‑like compounds in cocoa
items.content: Cocoa contains small amounts of theobromine, which may affect sleep in sensitive persons.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Reduced‑fat chocolate milk can be enjoyed chilled as a refreshing drink, blended into smoothies, used as a base for dessert sauces, or poured over oatmeal for a sweet twist. When heating, do so gently to avoid curdling the proteins.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the product refrigerated at 1 °C–4 °C. Once opened, consume within 3–5 days. Do not leave the milk at room temperature for more than 2 hours to prevent bacterial growth.
